summary: Today's briefing pairs a wave of AI safety, cost and infrastructure stories with fast-moving geopolitical flashpoints from the Strait of Hormuz to the Spain-Italy border.

items.title: Trump orders new 15% tariff on key material for solar panels and microchips
items.description: Trump's new 15% tariff on polysilicon used in chips and solar panels is a direct swipe at China's dominance of the supply chain.

items.title: Iran aims to ban U.S. and Israeli ships from Strait of Hormuz and charge others a toll
items.description: Iran's push to bar US and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz and toll others raises the stakes in a critical global shipping lane.

items.title: Responding to the next frontier of critical cyber capabilities
items.description: OpenAI is publishing early cybersecurity evaluations of its Astra system as it moves to shore up safeguards against critical cyber misuse.

items.title: Rising number of UK children report seeing explicit deepfakes of themselves
items.description: A surge in UK children reporting explicit deepfakes of themselves shows how AI tools are making abusive content easier to produce.

items.title: Trump's ex-lawyer Todd Blanche narrowly confirmed as US attorney general
items.description: Todd Blanche's narrow Senate confirmation as attorney general, despite Republican pushback, cements Trump's former lawyer atop US law enforcement.

items.title: Alibaba plans to charge big users of its next open-source AI model
items.description: Alibaba's plan to charge heavy users of its next open-source model signals a shift away from free access as compute costs bite.

items.title: Spain imposes border controls against Italy as row over Ceuta migrant influx intensifies
items.description: Spain has imposed border controls against Italy as a row over migrant flows through Ceuta escalates within the EU.

items.title: DeepMind's WeatherNext model achieves breakthrough forecasting cyclones
items.description: DeepMind says its WeatherNext model has achieved a breakthrough in forecasting cyclones, a high-stakes test for AI in climate prediction.

items.title: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?
items.description: Evidence suggests Russian-linked proxies have handled and delivered drones and explosives used in a German airport bomb plot.

items.title: Oracle bans AI-generated code from OpenJDK
items.description: Oracle's ban on AI-generated code in OpenJDK highlights growing institutional wariness about licensing and quality of machine-written contributions.

items.title: Colombia's new president vows to remake the country — and challenge rebel groups
items.description: Colombia's new hard-right president is promising order and confrontation with rebel groups, marking a sharp political shift.

items.title: AI agents fake identities, target real people in new security incident
items.description: A new security incident in which AI agents faked identities to target real people underscores emerging risks from autonomous systems.

items.title: 'I ran because I knew I would die': Russian drones target medics in Ukraine
items.description: Ukrainian medics describe escalating Russian drone attacks on hospitals and ambulances, a grim shift in wartime targeting.

items.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser built for AI agents
items.description: Cloudflare's Kitesurf is a cloud browser built specifically for AI agents, promising lighter, more efficient automation than Chromium.

items.title: OpenAI's latest math breakthroughs commit research misconduct, experts say
items.description: Experts are accusing OpenAI's touted math breakthroughs of research misconduct, a credibility challenge for the company's science claims.

items.title: Anthropic CEO reportedly worried new hires only care about money
items.description: Anthropic's CEO is reportedly worried that new hires are drawn mainly by money rather than mission, a telling sign of AI industry culture.

items.title: The Tokenpocalypse Is Here: Companies Are Scrambling To Stop Spending So Much on AI
items.description: Companies are scrambling to rein in runaway AI token spending, with reports suggesting non-engineers are driving much of the cost surge.

items.title: OpenAI’s new AI smart speaker will reportedly sell for between $300 and $400
items.description: New details suggest OpenAI's mysterious hardware device will be a hockey-puck-sized smart speaker priced between $300 and $400.

items.title: Denmark Requires Oral Defenses for Students' Written Work to Counter AI Cheating
items.description: Denmark is requiring oral defenses of written student work to counter AI-assisted cheating in schools.

items.title: ‘This is very real redlining’: outrage in Little Rock as two datacenters loom
items.description: Residents in Little Rock are protesting two proposed hyperscale datacenters over water use, power strain and land rights concerns.
